answer: Forging 55 aliases hence burns 453 bonds held for 14 days each, plus the umber attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single fable checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a sparrow, before it can post or attest. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
